Two rules that come out of this ledger:


1. Pushes and manual mentions draw from the same budget, and GitHub API is not the constraint (core used
   2 of 5000 at 16:52Z by write-response headers; /rate_limit itself lies about the counters).
2. Only spend a review on a head you intend to keep. Triggering a head and pushing it in the same hour
   pays twice - the review is dismissed and the new head needs another review.

## Correction after the probe (cr-trigger-probe-2489.md, 2026-11-22T17:0xZ)


The #2489 mention did **not** spend a bot review. The bot answered in about 5 seconds and refused: the
head was already reviewed, so `@coderabbitai review` is the wrong command, and it also said the command
only applies when automatic reviews are paused. Nothing started: no review event (latest coderabbitai
review is still CHANGES_REQUESTED from 2026-11-18T04:29:45Z), no check rows after 16:53:55Z, threads
unchanged at 3/1 open, gate still pending since 2026-11-18T04:44:58Z. Cost was 2 core points only.

So the honest window arithmetic is: 1 spent (#2450 fresh approval at 16:24:20Z), about 3 left. The
push-hold on #2489 that I ordered on the "wasted review" premise is lifted: pushing 2b70528c0 now is the
productive move, because the push itself dismisses the stale CHANGES_REQUESTED, re-runs the six required
checks and re-triggers a review of the head that actually contains the fix.

What is not observable, stated plainly: the bot reply carries no quota number, no reset timestamp and no
Retry-After. The only signals available are the reply wording itself (queued, refused, paused) and time.
Schedule against the ~4/hour figure in zoo-stack-maintenance, spend it in the order dirty-order.md gives,
and read the refusal wording as the traffic light - it is the closest thing to a meter this channel has.
